title: 2023 budget approved with 5.45% property tax increase
subtitle: Sidewalk snow clearing review, earthquake relief donation, new staff positions, capital plan, and failed budget menu items.
overview: Council approved the 2023 operating budget with an average property tax increase of 5.45% over 2022 and a total levy of $92,656,663 {{vote:m99}}. It also approved the 2023 capital budget of $98,557,000 and, in principle, a 2024 to 2032 capital forecast {{vote:m93}}. Staff said the budget includes efficiencies and was prepared amid high inflation and interest rates.

Council added a construction supervisor position and used extra assessment growth to offset costs. It did not approve three optional items: more affordable housing funding, more infrastructure reserve funding, and Microsoft licences for staff without city email. The licence motion ended in a tie, which means it failed.

Council directed staff to report back before June 2023 on improving sidewalk snow clearing, for consideration in the 2024 to 2026 budget. Council also approved a $10,000 donation to the Canadian Red Cross for earthquake relief in Türkiye and Syria. Council met in closed session before the public meeting, and the minutes report no public outcome from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved the 2023 operating budget with an average property tax increase of 5.45% and a total levy of $92,656,663 {{vote:m99}}.
Council approved the $98,557,000 2023 capital budget and, in principle, the 2024 to 2032 capital forecast totalling $750,721,000 {{vote:m93}}.
Staff must report back before June 2023 on options for improving sidewalk snow clearing, focused on key corridors and transit, schools and health facilities, for the 2024 to 2026 budget {{vote:m15}}.
Council donated $10,000 from its Community Priority and Contingency Reserve to the Canadian Red Cross for earthquake relief in Türkiye and Syria {{vote:m101}}.
Council added an ongoing $145,000 for a permanent Construction Supervisor in Facilities Design and Management Services {{vote:m50}}.
A proposed $100,000 annual increase for affordable housing did not pass {{vote:m52}}.
A proposed additional $434,000 for the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund did not pass {{vote:m53}}.
A $90,000 request for Microsoft licences for staff without city email failed on a tied vote {{vote:m54}}.

debate: Sidewalk snow clearing: the mayor said delegates and residents had raised the issue and pointed to transit and accessibility. One councillor asked for a council engagement session before staff report back. Staff said engagement would use the online survey platform and the new committees of council.

Affordable housing: some councillors preferred to wait for the affordable housing strategy due March 20. They noted the provincial development charge exemptions and the region's larger role. One councillor argued the strategy would need more money than planned.

Infrastructure funding: staff said extra money would help close the infrastructure funding gap and avoid costlier repairs later. Opponents pointed to affordability for residents on fixed incomes. Staff said an update to the long-term financial plan is coming.

Microsoft licences: staff said some employees lack city email and use personal accounts, which raises cyber security and freedom-of-information concerns and could help engagement. One councillor asked whether the item could wait for the 2024 employee survey.

Construction supervisor: staff said the role is currently a contract position that is about to end. They said it covers site oversight, health and safety, coordination with programs, and accessibility work.
